The course provides a powerful lens for understanding how gender shapes global politics in both visible and invisible ways. It introduces key theoretical frameworks clearly, while also grounding them in real-world cases such as feminist foreign policy, gendered conflict dynamics, and women’s political participation. The discussions are engaging and intellectually stimulating, encouraging students to challenge assumptions and think critically about global power structures. The readings are diverse, intersectional, and thought-provoking, opening space for perspectives from the Global South as well as contemporary debates. All in all I would say, the course greatly strengthens analytical skills and widens one’s understanding of how gender influences international relations. If anything could be improved, it would simply be creating more balance between the heavy reading load and the time available to fully digest the material. Some topics are incredibly rich and could benefit from a slower pace, more guided discussion, or additional examples to help students connect theory to practice, and this could be done by giving maybe one book for two weeks, instead of a new book every week.
